submission.natural_language_explanation: Fuzzy induction head: it fires at a token whose spelling already occurred earlier in the context - the same token, a case variant (' WHITWORTH' after ' Whitworth'), a space variant (' EN' after '(EN'), an inflection ('tractors' after 'tractor') or a word piece ('IT' after ' Whit', 'ENS' after 'MAX_TOKENS') - and at its peaks it puts 0.7-1.0 of its attention on the token that immediately followed that earlier occurrence, copying it into the residual (a second 'Vessel' copies '.', a second 'if' copies "'s", the 'M' of 'low-URM' copies ' schools'). A repeat of a name, acronym, number, identifier or subword piece, or of a content word inside a repeated multi-token phrase, usually reaches 6-21 strength (above the 5.2 line), while a function word or punctuation mark that recurs with different neighbours in ordinary prose stays at the floor (0-4), as do a token's first occurrence, a word with no earlier spelling match, and a different word that shares no piece with an earlier one ('Whitney' after 'Whitworth').

rival_explanations: Generic in-context repeat detector: it fires on any token that has already appeared earlier in the context, common function words and punctuation included, copying whatever came next; on this reading the strong examples only look distinctive because the corpus rarely repeats ordinary words with a sharp match.

Name and acronym copier: it fires only on repetitions of proper names, acronyms, numbers and code identifiers, and not on ordinary repeated content words ('tractor', 'cat', 'green') or repeated multi-token sentences.
